- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward to reflect stronger bearish momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a lagged correction by reducing forecast by 10–15% of the spike magnitude.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 1–3 day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for short-term bias.
- In long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, apply a downward bias of 1–3% to reflect volatility decay.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or negative), model tends to ignore trend; increase forecast sensitivity to recent price action, especially if prices are trending.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over 3+ days, model overreacts to short-term noise; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
